intro_md:
Written on 29 September 2026. This records the line pass made outside this repository on 28–29 September, in the conversation summarised in `New - Re-plan/Claude Handoff.md` (§3). The author accepted every change, and the chapter now matches the text they supplied.

The chapter as it stood before the pass is saved unchanged as `Drafts/Chapter 2 - The Price of a Voice (Draft 3, before the line pass).md`, and every change here is measured against it. The rounds before the pass are in `Chapter 2 - Changes.md`. **Round 2** (29 September) is an edit folded into change 9. **Later rounds go on this list** (`Drafts/Chapter 2 - change list (line pass).json`).

Each reason says where it comes from: the handoff when it gives one, or Claude's reading when it doesn't. Changes tagged as the author's own lines replaced something the author wrote or designed; they are listed below, under "The author's own lines this pass replaced".
summary_md:
## The author's own lines this pass replaced

Changes {tag:authorline}. The handoff records them as accepted. They are listed here because the skill asks that every change to the author's own lines be flagged.

changes.title: The elf at the door
changes.before: "Farmer, answer this damn door before we start knocking down others because of your silence."
changes.after: "Open the door, farmer. Keep us waiting, and yours won't be the only one we knock down tonight."
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the elf sounds sure of himself, and the threat to the neighbours comes as an aside, which is how Decisions.md describes the elves ("cocky and full of themselves"). This replaces the author's own example line from Decisions.md ("Farmer, answer this damn door before we start knocking down others because of your silence").
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The choking
changes.before: Air bubbled out around the blade. A thick, wet clicking filled his throat, and every breath he took brought up more blood, frothing pink at his lips and running down the steel into the collar of his armour. He choked on it. He choked again, and his heels scraped at the boards, and the hand on Gerolt's wrist began to shake.
changes.after: Air bubbled around the blade. A wet clicking filled his throat while blood frothed over his lips and ran down the steel into his collar. His heels scraped at the boards, and the hand on Gerolt's wrist began to shake.
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "The violent details were compressed where several sentences repeated the same physical failure."
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Her armour
changes.before: She stood beside the horses with one hand thrust towards the cabin. The same dark armour, lighter, under a grey travelling cloak. Her pale hair had come loose across a face twisted with disbelief.
changes.after: She stood beside the horses with one hand thrust towards the cabin. She wore the same dark armour beneath a grey travelling cloak. Her pale hair had come loose across a face twisted with disbelief.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the fragment ("The same dark armour, lighter, under a grey travelling cloak.") becomes a plain sentence.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: Something cracked
changes.before: A slab of soil and rock slammed into Gerolt's chest and threw him back through the doorway. He hit the floor hard enough to shake the whole cabin, and the boy heard something inside him crack. The sword skidded away across the boards and stopped an arm's length from the boy's hand.
changes.after: A slab of soil and rock slammed into Gerolt's chest and threw him back through the doorway. He hit the floor hard enough to shake the whole cabin, and the boy heard something crack. The sword skidded away across the boards and stopped an arm's length from the boy's hand.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the boy hears something crack, but can't know it was inside Gerolt. Point of view.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The words broke into a cough
changes.before: "I know." It broke into a cough. Gerolt curled around his side until it passed, blood shining between his teeth.
changes.after: "I know." The words broke into a cough. Gerolt curled around his side until it passed, blood shining between his teeth.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): "It" could be read as Gerolt's side. The author's rule: make "it" clear.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The ride's last thought
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the spiral on the ride already turns three times (why he killed him, why they came, why he burnt the house). The fourth turn asked "what is happening" again without a new claim (principle 8). "What is happening" was part of the author's own rough thought for the ride.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The sword
changes.before: He held it out to Alaric hilt first. Alaric didn't take it. He had watched Gerolt fight with that sword tonight. If he took it, Gerolt wasn't coming, and he would be facing them with his bare hands. He would die here. Gerolt pressed it into his hands anyway and closed his fingers around the grip.
changes.after: He held it out to Alaric hilt first. Alaric didn't take it. He had watched Gerolt fight with that sword tonight. Taking it meant leaving Gerolt to face them bare-handed. It meant watching him die here. Gerolt pressed the hilt into Alaric's hands anyway and forced his fingers around it.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the author's meaning from round 3 is kept (he watched Gerolt fight with it; giving it away means Gerolt faces them bare-handed and dies), now put as what taking it would mean to Alaric.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: He finished with a cough
changes.before: It ended in a small cough, and blood began to run from the corner of his mouth.
changes.after: He finished with a small cough, and blood began to run from the corner of his mouth.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): "It ended" becomes a sentence that starts from Gerolt.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: He can't move
changes.before:
*What do I do?*

He had a sword in one hand. In the other he was holding on to a dog.

*I could—no. No, I can't. I can't do anything. I want to help him, and I can't even make my legs move. I'm scared. If I go down there, they'll kill me. I'll die. I don't want to die. I don't want to—*
changes.after:
He tried to go back down to Gerolt, but his legs just wouldn't move.

*If I go down there, they'll kill me. I don't want to die. I don't want to—*
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "Alaric now attempts to move during the final stand and fails physically, rather than only explaining inside his head that he is unable to act." His thought keeps its last turn ("I don't want to die"). The author's rough thought for this moment was "What do I do, I can't do anything, I want to help, I can't, I'm scared to help, I will die, I don't want to die." **Round 2 (29 September):** the line pass had him "try to stand" three paragraphs after he stopped on his feet. Claude's first fix was "robotic"; the author's idea was "He tried to continue moving, ever closer towards Gerolt, but his legs just won't move", and of the two options built from it the author chose B.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3). Round 2: the author chose option B (29 September).

changes.title: Alaric couldn't get up
changes.before: Alaric couldn't get up. He was staring at Gerolt. That old man had taken care of him until his dying breath, and now Alaric was going to leave him there and never see him again.
changes.after: Alaric couldn't get up. Gerolt had taken care of him until his dying breath, and now Alaric was going to leave him there and never see him again.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the author's own line from round 2 is trimmed: "He was staring at Gerolt" and "That old man" go, and what Gerolt did for him stays in Alaric's understanding.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).
